bounded_slice.candidate: RFC 8949 core deterministic CBOR as the stable byte-serialization profile for evidence payloads embedded in COSE_Sign1
bounded_slice.tested_scope: Static inspection of exactly one official RFC Editor primary source, RFC 8949. Tested only whether a fixed evidence data structure can be serialized under an explicit deterministic CBOR profile to stable byte-identical payload bytes suitable for embedding as the COSE_Sign1 payload. No encoder implementation, second public source, external service, protected-primary action, manual-user execution, scheduler mutation, or other-worker/downstream/O semantic input was consumed.
observations: RFC 8949 states that protocols can require a deterministic CBOR format and defines restrictions that can serve as its base.

The core deterministic requirements require preferred shortest serialization, forbid indefinite-length items, and require every map's keys to be sorted by the bytewise lexicographic order of their deterministic encodings.

These rules remove major wire-level degrees of freedom for a fixed CBOR data-model value: integer/length/tag arguments use shortest forms, floating-point values use the shortest form preserving the value, containers are definite-length, and map ordering is fixed.

RFC 8949 also warns that deterministic encoding can require application-profile choices beyond the core rules when the same application semantics admit multiple CBOR data-model representations, including tag present/absent choices, integer-versus-float choices, NaN representation, signed zero, decimal/bigfloat alternatives, or other numeric forms.

Therefore core deterministic CBOR is sufficient for stable payload bytes only after the evidence profile itself fixes or excludes semantic representation ambiguities; the RFC does not by itself define the evidence schema or those application-level choices.
bounded_slice.inference: Specification-level conditional pass for the canonical-payload child: an evidence package whose application schema fixes a single CBOR data-model representation and applies RFC 8949 core deterministic encoding can be serialized to stable byte-identical bytes suitable for the embedded COSE_Sign1 payload identified in p1-sa-556. This closes neither the evidence schema nor every application-level normalization rule; without such a fixed profile, semantically equivalent evidence may still encode to different deterministic CBOR byte strings.
bounded_slice.uncertainty: No implementation or byte-for-byte interoperability test was executed. No claim is made that arbitrary JSON/PROV/evidence objects automatically have a unique CBOR representation, that a scheduled Chat surface exposes a conforming deterministic encoder, or that cryptographic signing/key trust/replay policy is solved.
